cause: Context Pack was frozen before development started.
impact: The line has an evidence-bound starting context.
lesson: Freeze the initial context before changing implementation state.

cause: A read-only fixture inspection invoked the unavailable python command instead of the repository interpreter.
impact: The command failed before reading or writing the fixture; no repository state changed.
lesson: Use the repository interpreter from the frozen Context Pack for every fixture and gate command.

cause: The first read-only hash command failed in the shell locale setup before producing a digest.
impact: No repository file was read or written by the failed hash command; the same digest check succeeded after setting the supported locale.
lesson: Set the supported LC_ALL and LANG values before repository verification commands.

cause: The implementation plan declares v1-8-9-p0-workflow-truth-core, v1-8-9-p0-evidence-core, and v1-8-9-p0-agent-compiler-core dependencies, but their formal handoffs and retrospectives are absent at baseline c9f3c4ed3e07faf6f57f795a5e35fa6f8042c749.
impact: C1 producer/runtime integration cannot be claimed. The minimum slice must consume the locked C0 EvidencePersistencePortV1 seam, preserve missing or restricted facts, and keep the absent dependency boundary explicit.
lesson: When C1 producers are absent, keep consumer projections port-based and fail closed; never reimplement dependency internals.

cause: The first append attempt used a UTC RFC3339 timestamp without millisecond precision and was rejected by the formal event validator.
impact: The GAP was not appended on the first attempt; no implementation file was changed, and the corrected GAP append succeeded immediately afterward.
lesson: Use millisecond-precision UTC RFC3339 timestamps for every formal event source.

cause: The first focused TDD run collected the newly added projection tests before the owned consumer_adapters and coverage modules existed, so the expected imports failed with ModuleNotFoundError.
impact: This is the intentional red phase of TDD; no production implementation had been written yet and no protected or P1 path changed.
lesson: Run the focused contract tests before implementation and preserve the red result as evidence of the test-first boundary.

cause: The first append attempt for the TDD red event used an unsupported preventability value and was rejected by the formal event validator.
impact: The red event was not appended on the first attempt; the source was corrected and the append succeeded without changing implementation state.
lesson: Use only the formal preventability vocabulary already present in the line event stream.

cause: The first implementation sorted persisted NumericFactV1 values by fact_id for every consumer, while the cross-consumer contract requires the source envelope identity and ordering to remain unchanged.
impact: Two focused assertions failed: cross-consumer fact order and budget omission order. No fact values were recalculated or changed.
lesson: A projection ordering declaration must not silently reorder a persisted envelope when same-source identity includes sequence; preserve the envelope sequence in the minimal port slice.

cause: The newly added frontend contract test supplied a typed evidence projection while FamilyEvidence still had only the legacy family-model branch, so React rendered no typed projection element.
impact: The three existing legacy FamilyEvidence tests remained green; only the new typed contribution test was red before its owned contribution was implemented.
lesson: Add typed consumer UI contributions behind an explicit prop and keep legacy report behavior unchanged.

cause: The first reportEvidence contribution replaced an existing shared module instead of preserving its groupFacts, capability-manifest, and display-label exports used by legacy report consumers.
impact: The first frontend typecheck reported missing exports across existing report consumers. The original exports were restored by compatibility-preserving apply_patch before continuing; no protected ReportView file was edited.
lesson: When an owned module already has public consumers, extend its API additively and preserve every existing export.

cause: The focused frontend typecheck still fails because an existing untracked ClassificationEvidence.test.tsx imports missing ClassificationEvidence.tsx; that source is outside this line's owned paths and is not present at baseline.
impact: The owned FamilyEvidence focused test is green, but repository-wide frontend typecheck cannot be claimed. The missing classification source is not repaired in this line.
lesson: Keep unrelated missing consumer sources as an explicit known gate and do not expand an owned-path scope to repair them.

cause: The source-order regression was traced to the adapter's fact_id sort and corrected by iterating the persisted envelope sequence; no value transformation or statistical recomputation was introduced.
impact: The cross-consumer identity/value/order assertions and budget omission-order assertions are green; the earlier source-order failure is resolved.
lesson: Review the persisted sequence boundary explicitly whenever a projection declares an ordering policy.

cause: The port-based consumer projection slice completed its focused backend, frontend, and Python compilation checks after the source-order correction.

impact.typecheck: open GAP: existing ClassificationEvidence.test.tsx imports missing out-of-scope ClassificationEvidence.tsx

lesson: Keep focused projection evidence separate from repository-wide typecheck and downstream mount acceptance.

cause: The line Context Pack and event chain verified successfully, and git diff --check reported no whitespace errors after the bounded implementation and handoff were generated.
impact: Formal process control and diff hygiene are verified; browser, runtime mounts, repository-wide frontend typecheck, full gate, and release evidence remain explicitly outside this gate.
lesson: Complete formal verification and diff hygiene before line close, while preserving downstream acceptance boundaries as separate evidence.

cause: The bounded C0 port-based consumer projection slice, focused tests, handoff, formal verification, and diff check are complete. The missing C1 handoffs and out-of-scope classification source remain explicit open limits.
impact: The line closes as a verified implementation slice, not as a production cutover or release. Open GAPs remain visible in the event stream and handoff.
lesson: Close a bounded line only when its local contract and process evidence are complete, while keeping missing producers and downstream acceptance as open limits.

cause: After the final additive import correction, the focused backend projection/coverage suite, focused FamilyEvidence suite, Python compileall, git diff check, and formal line verification were rerun successfully.

impact.typecheck: not verified; open out-of-scope ClassificationEvidence source GAP

lesson: Re-run the focused evidence after the last code edit and keep the repository-wide typecheck boundary explicit.
